messages.author: 1ec3f8d9a5847ab4
messages.subject: Multidimensional between-item CAT (MCAT)
parts:
Hi Phil,

I'm trying to adapt/simulate a personality test (14 distinct, but intercorrelated dimensions from 210 polytomous items) as a CAT from real data in 3 steps. My goal is to study the efficiency of CAT in comparison to linear testing for this questionnaire.

First I interpreted each dimension as an unidimensional factor, separated the items into 14 different datasets, fitted 14 unidimensional GRM-models and administered 14 independent UCATs. Up to this point, that worked well: The UCATs need only around 50% of the items in average.

Now second I want to run an MCAT with all 14 dimensions and the compete dataset, but uncorrelated, so as to compare the results to step 1. I fitted a mirt-model like this:

model <- 'F1 =  7, 22, 37, 53, 69, 85, 100, 115, 130, 144, 159, 172, 196, 204

                 F2 =  8, 23, 38, 54, 70, 86, 101, 116, 131, 145, 173, 186

                 F3 =  9, 24, 39, 55, 71, 87, 102, 117, 132, 146, 160, 174, 187, 197, 205

                 F4 =  11, 26, 41, 57, 73, 89, 104, 119, 134, 148, 162, 176, 188, 206

                 F5 =  12, 27, 42, 58, 74, 90, 105, 120, 135, 149, 163, 177, 189, 198

                 F6 =  13, 28, 43, 59, 75, 91, 106, 121, 136, 150, 164, 178, 190, 199

                 F7 =  14, 29, 44, 60, 76, 92, 107, 122, 151, 165, 179, 191

                 F8 =  2, 16, 31, 46, 62, 78, 94, 109, 124, 138, 153, 167, 181, 192, 201, 208

                 F9=  1, 15, 30, 45, 61, 77, 93, 108, 123, 137, 152, 166, 180, 200, 207

                 F10 =  3, 17, 32, 47, 63, 79, 95, 110, 125, 139, 154, 168, 182

                 F11 =  10, 25, 40, 56, 72, 88, 103, 118, 133, 147, 161, 175

                 F12 =  4, 18, 33, 48, 64, 80, 96, 111, 126, 140, 155, 169, 183, 193, 202, 209

                 F13 =  5, 19, 34, 49, 65, 81, 97, 112, 127, 141, 156, 170, 184

                 F14 =  6, 20, 35, 50, 66, 82, 98, 113, 128, 142, 157, 171, 185, 194, 203, 210'


Generated the mirt-model like:

mirt.model <- mirt(data, model = model, 'graded', cl = cl, method = "MHRM")


And ran the MCAT like this:

cat.design <- list(min_items = 5, min_SEM = 0.35, delta_thetas = 0.05) #Same as in UCATs

result <- mirtCAT(mo = mirt.model, local_pattern = data.pattern, start_item = 'Drule', criteria = 'Drule', design = cat.design) 


Yet, the thetas of the MCAT for each factor are not remotely comparable to the results of the different UCATs from step 1. There are only around 20 items from 210 selected, SE is quite high (NOT around .35 as wanted). I would have guessed the MCAT would work quite similar to a bunch of UCATs when the factors are treated as uncorrelated. Can you spot my mistake? Is there a way to tell mirtCAT to use the termination criteria (like min_item = 5) for each factor separately?


Then for step 3, I want to repeat the MCAT but with respect to the intercorrelations of the dimensions. As those are quite highly correlated, I expect an even better efficiency in comparison to step 1 and 2. How can I include the intercorrelations into my model? I assume something like 'COV = F1*F2*...*F14' in the model definition - is that correct? Is there a possibility to tell mirt specific correlations/covarinces (for example as a cov-matrix)?


Additionally, I am quite confused with the selection-criteria argument in mirtCAT. With UCATs I use 'MI' for maximum information - which criteria should I use equivalently in MCAT? Is there any literature where I can read about the differences of Drule, Trule, APrule etc.?


I would be very thankful for your help!

Best wishes

Nick

How close were the multidimensional item parameters to the unidimensional ones that you calibrated? The MIRT models are not really free to estimate as the integrals have to be evaluated using stochastic estimation. Plus, the selection criteria is slightly different (determinant rule is trying to pick items that minimize the overall volume of the measurement uncertainty, rather than a single unidimensional slice). 

Regarding your follow-up questions, mirtCAT doesn't support termination based on single factor criteria like min_items for each dimension, but you could certainly do this if you use some of the customization functions that you can define yourself.

Have you seen the associated JSS paper discussing the theory behind mirtCAT? That might be a good place to start. HTH.

Phil

messages.subject: Re: Multidimensional between-item CAT (MCAT)
parts:
Hi Phil,

I'm very thankful for your help and quite sorry to bother you again! 

As you suggested, I'm currently trying to work with the customNextItem()-Function in order to archive a min_items criteria for each factor.
To do that I'm creating a counter object (data frame with rows = nfact) that is increased by the customNextItem() by +1 for the specific factor each time an item is chosen. I then can break the MCAT by returning NA, if !any(counter < min_items). This is realized through an (external/additional) object in my global environment, which is deleted and reestablished after every person. 

Unfortunately, this solution is merely a work-around and has at least to flaws: 1. It is prone to error when the external counter is not correctly deleted and reestablished for a new person and 2. I cannot directly access the counter through the person object during or after MCAT since it's not connected to each other (meaning the counter is not bound to a specific person). It would be nice to have a more robust solution as well as the possibility to access the counter post-CAT for evaluation.

Hence my new question: Do you know any possibility to add and save this counter as a field in the person-object? I haven't yet found a possibility to add a field to an instance of a reference class object by the customNextItem function. Or maybe you know a more elegant solution to my problem other than working with an additional object in the global environment?

Last question: You told me MCAT is not supporting termination based on single factor criteria like min_items for each dimension. Yet with extract.mirtCAT(x = design, what = "met_SEM") I get a vector with logical values for each factor. So unlike min_items, min_SEM is supported for MCAT? What about delta_thetas?

Thank you very much in advance and best wishes!
Nick

I like the idea of users including their own customized object slot information, ideally in the form of a list for generality purposes. I'll add this to the TODO list and hopefully have it implemented for the next major release (also long overdue....).

Last question: You told me MCAT is not supporting termination based on single factor criteria like min_items for each dimension. The min_SEM criteria in MCAT does work, it's the min_items per dimension that does not. Hence, you'd need to define your own way of tracking this information as a function of the loadings pattern + items responded to (related to your counter tracking suggestion). 

Phil

Thank you very much in advance and best wishes!
Nick
